output:
**What I found:** The requirement holds up: Product confirmed the problem, a support count backs it, and the done state and out-of-scope list are clear. The decision is to treat it as ready for the next stage (the record calls this GROUNDED), but the next stage is not dependency modeling yet: the pipeline puts the build-or-not decision first, and the only stated reason to build is a ticket reduction that nobody has measured or given a target.

**Why it matters:** If you skip the build decision, the work gets modeled and built on the expected ticket drop without knowing how many of the ~120 monthly tickets a self-serve path would actually replace. If you hold it until the expectation has a number, that decision rests on evidence rather than on what the head of support expects.

**Do this first:**
1. In the ticket system, have the support lead classify one month of the ~120 past-invoice tickets by who asked (account owner or someone else) and what they asked for (an invoice or a credit note). The share from account owners asking for an invoice is the most the requirement could remove.
2. Have the head of support set the smallest drop in tickets that would justify the work, then run `/functionality-complexity-tradeoff`.
3. If that returns BUILD, run `/requirements-topology` on the three candidates below.

**What I did not check:**
- I didn't see the ticket data, so the ~120/month figure and how it was counted are as you stated them. To close it, export the category from the ticket system.
- Whether every past invoice is still stored and can be retrieved. To close it, ask the billing data owner for the retention policy.
- Whether anyone other than the account owner can see invoices today. To close it, ask product for the current access rules on invoices.
- Whether any legal source (privacy or invoice retention law) applies. To close it, review with legal or compliance.

```text
Subject:        Past-invoice self-service for account owners (invoicing product)
Mode:           conversational
Decision:       GROUNDED
Problem:        An account owner (actor) who needs a past invoice for bookkeeping (situation)
                must be able to obtain it (outcome) but today can only get it by contacting
                support (obstacle). Confirmed by Product.
Basis profile:  1 evidenced (past-invoice-retrieval), 2 interpreted (invoice-copy-fidelity,
                invoice-access-unchanged); 1 outcome hypothesis, hypothesized
Confidence:     high (problem and core requirement); medium (the two interpreted candidates)
Blocking gaps:  None for grounding. The hypothesis has no threshold and no addressable share;
                it blocks M's worth verdict, not grounding.
Outcome hypotheses: support-ticket-deflection, unmeasured, confidence low
Supersedes:     none
Next action:    Size the addressable share and get a threshold from the head of support, then
                run functionality-complexity-tradeoff (M). Run requirements-topology only after
                M returns BUILD.
Verification:   Checked the problem statement, done state, and out-of-scope list against the
                Problem Check; ran the quality sweep. Not run: ticket data, invoice retention,
                current access rules (no source available).
Revisit when:   M verdict is issued, or the addressable-share sample is done
```

**Problem:** An account owner who needs a past invoice for bookkeeping cannot get it without contacting support.
**Done when:** An account owner can obtain any invoice issued to their account without contacting support.
**Not the problem:** Changing what an invoice contains, credit notes, and access for anyone other than the account owner.

**Requirement candidates**

```text
Requirement: past-invoice-retrieval
Actor: Account owner
Must be able to: obtain a copy of any invoice issued to their account without contacting support
So that: they can complete their bookkeeping
Complete when:
- For a test account with invoices from its first to its latest, the owner obtains each one
  with no support contact
- The oldest invoice issued to the account can be obtained the same way as the newest
Basis: evidenced
Source or evidence: support lead's count (~120 tickets/month over the last 3 months); Product confirmation
Priority: must
Validation decision: accept
Confidence: high
```

```text
Requirement: invoice-copy-fidelity
Actor: Account owner
Must be able to: obtain a copy whose content matches the invoice as it was issued
So that: the copy is valid for bookkeeping
Complete when:
- For a sample of issued invoices, every field on the obtained copy matches the issued invoice
Basis: interpreted (from "changing what an invoice contains" being out of scope, plus the bookkeeping purpose)
Priority: must
Validation decision: test (Product to confirm the reading)
Confidence: medium
```

```text
Requirement: invoice-access-unchanged
Actor: Account owner
Must be able to: rely on their invoices not becoming available to anyone who could not
                 already get them
Complete when:
- No user other than the account owner gains access to an invoice they could not get before
- A non-owner who tries to get another account's invoice is refused
Basis: interpreted (from "access for anyone other than the account owner" being out of scope; legal basis unverified)
Priority: must
Validation decision: test (Product to confirm; legal review open)
Confidence: medium
```

**Outcome hypothesis**

```text
Outcome hypothesis: support-ticket-deflection
Applies to requirements: past-invoice-retrieval
Actor or cohort: Support team; account owners who currently file past-invoice tickets
If: account owners can obtain past invoices themselves
Then: past-invoice tickets per month go down
Because: those tickets exist only because there is no other way to get the invoice
Primary measure: past-invoice tickets per month (lower is better)
Baseline: ~120/month total (manual count, last 3 months); addressable share unknown
Decision threshold: unknown (owner: head of support)
Evaluation window: unknown (owner: head of support)
Guardrails: invoice-access incidents stay at zero; other ticket categories do not rise
Evidence plan: tag the category consistently in the ticket system; classify a one-month sample
               by requester role and request type before building; compare before and after release
Hypothesis confidence: low
Evidence state: unmeasured
Evidence reference: none
Owner: head of support
Revisit when: sample is classified, or a threshold is set
```

**Quality coverage**
- **Functional suitability:** covered by past-invoice-retrieval and invoice-copy-fidelity. Open, owned by Product: whether "any invoice" includes corrected, voided, or pre-migration invoices; how to handle closed accounts; how to handle owners of several accounts.
- **Security (confidentiality):** covered by invoice-access-unchanged. Open, owned by legal: whether privacy law applies.
- **Reliability:** open, owned by the billing data owner: are all issued invoices still retained? This is a risk to the "any invoice" done state.
- **Compatibility:** open, owned by Product: what file format bookkeeping needs.
- **Interaction capability (inclusivity):** open, owned by Product: which accessibility standard applies.
- **Performance:** not applicable. Nothing in the sources sets a time limit, and support remains as a fallback.
- **Maintainability and flexibility:** not applicable at grounding; these are design-stage questions.
- **Safety:** not applicable. No harm to people, property, or the environment is involved.

**Watch items**
- The 3-month count may be seasonal, since bookkeeping often peaks around period close.
- The count was done by hand, so it may include requests from non-owners or for credit notes, which this work would not cover.

**Topology handoff note:** Three candidates. invoice-copy-fidelity and invoice-access-unchanged both constrain past-invoice-retrieval. Neither has `Holds across`, because both apply to this one scope only.
